clue.text: Food the Italian way — no dish, oddly, needed

parts.note: via is the Italian word for a way or road

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the words no dish

explanation.surface: Eating Italian-style needs no plate at all, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd-placed letters of NO DISH: N, D and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Viands is an old word for provisions or items of food.

clue.text: Vehicle insurance that's highly acceptable in North American city

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: in puts the acceptable letter inside the insurance word

parts.note: cover is insurance
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Car insurance is very acceptable in a certain North American city.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, hence socially acceptable, is an old convention from the U and non-U debate about British speech; 'in' puts it inside the insurance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Recall a ringleader forming a ring

parts.note: to recall a decision is to revoke or annul it
the leader of the word ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ringleader is recalled for forming a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped.

clue.text: It's loosely associated with talented amateur

indicators.note: loosely suggests the letters are put together in a free, rearranged order

parts.note: the word it, with 's as a link for is

explanation.surface: It is loosely linked to gifted amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges IT + TALENTED; 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject as an amateur.

clue.text: Jack may be seen here — in box and pack of cards

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A jack might turn up in a box or in a pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor (jack tar), not the playing card the surface suggests; the spar-deck is an upper deck of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor, or jack tar, would be found on the upper deck of a ship.

clue.text: Hands on most of the business the French passed up

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter of the business word

parts.note: a practice is a professional business

indicators.note: passed up in a down clue means the piece is read upwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: The French passed up a hands-on business.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical means involving actual doing rather than theory, as hands-on does.

clue.text: Unusual choice

definitions.meaning: choice means of fine quality, excellent

explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon, and in older use exceptionally fine.

clue.text: English chap turned up at our entrance

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English fellow turned up at our front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway; MAN turned up gives NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to charm them, to make them fall in love.

clue.text: Boat unaffected by capsizing

indicators.note: a word unaffected by being turned over reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A boat that is not harmed by turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a palindrome, and a kayak can roll and right itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small enclosed canoe.

clue.text: Employer's conduct not hard-hearted

indicators.note: not hard-hearted means removing the letter for hard from the middle

parts.note: to usher is to conduct someone

explanation.surface: An employer's behaviour is not cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: H (hard) comes out of the middle of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: No advantage's allowed in new puzzle

indicators.note: the phrase has allowed in says the first pieces let the next letter come inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a plus is an advantage; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: No advantage is permitted for a newcomer, which is baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or perplex them.

clue.text: Early, perhaps — coming round a day before now

indicators.note: coming round says the rearranged letters circle the next pieces
perhaps suggests the letters of early in some other possible order

explanation.surface: Someone arriving early, perhaps, comes round a day ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of Early, and 'coming round' wraps that rearrangement around A plus the day letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, earlier than expected.

clue.text: Destroy book after nothing gets learned

indicators.note: after places the book letter following the nothing letter

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, nothing
literate means educated, learned

explanation.surface: A book is ruined after nobody bothers to learn from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy completely.

clue.text: Fashion business

definitions.meaning: to fashion something is to shape or ... it

explanation.definitionFit: Work as a verb means to shape material; as a noun it means one's occupation.

clue.text: Open committee meeting up stairs?

parts.note: upstairs is above
a board is a committee

explanation.surface: An open committee meets upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The board meets above, which gives the answer when the two are put the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Above-board means honest and open, without concealment.

clue.text: Five song-books, altogether different

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an aria is a song in an opera
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Five songbooks, each entirely unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a standard crossword source for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is a form that differs from the standard one.

clue.text: Tough assignment class has proudly taken on

parts.note: to stand or walk tall is to carry oneself proudly
an order is a class or rank

explanation.surface: A class has proudly taken on a difficult task.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is a request that is hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Guy in jazz club hosting strip show

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cat is jazz slang for a man, a hip guy
to bare is to strip

explanation.surface: A man in a jazz club is putting on a striptease.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment, a floor show.

clue.text: Count embraces ambassador jolly warmly

indicators.note: embraces means the count word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: to tally is to count
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A nobleman hugs a cheerful ambassador warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is TALLY; Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermally means by means of heat, so in a warm way.

clue.text: Write article about a telling performance

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of article are moved around

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a piece about a compelling show.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a telling or narration, and also a musical performance.

clue.text: Originally all the sailors imprisoned for butchery

annotationWithheld.why: Originally all the sailors imprisoned for butchery: A + RN must go into CAGE, but no clue word gives CAGE except imprisoned, which would also have to be the insertion indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Originally all the sailors imprisoned for butchery

clue.text: Nothing about a heartless betrayal is attractive

indicators.note: about says the nothing word wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: love means nil, nothing, in tennis scoring

indicators.note: heartless removes all the inner letters of betrayal, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Being entirely without a heartless betrayal makes a person appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis; 'heartless' strips betrayal to its first and last letters, and 'about' wraps the nothing word round A plus those.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovable means easy to love, endearing and attractive.

clue.text: Inspiring passages?

parts.note: inspiring read literally is breathing in, and passages are tubes for air in the lungs, not stirring bits of text

explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the main airways branching from the windpipe into the lungs.

clue.text: Share a concern

definitions.meaning: a share is a portion or ...
a ... is one's role or concern in a matter

explanation.definitionFit: Part means a portion of something, and also one's role or involvement.

clue.text: Dad and Mum have a meeting in the Turk's Head

parts.note: pa is a word for father, dad
mum as in keep mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Mother and Father meet in a pub called the Turk's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but silence (keep mum): SH. The Turk's Head looks like a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking official, a governor or head in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: May do well, having Joyce's personality

parts.note: May and Molly are both pet forms of Mary, so one girl's name stands for the other
to bloom is to flourish, to do well

explanation.surface: A girl might do well if she has the character of a Joyce heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the verb but is a girl's name; Ulysses is James Joyce's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Molly Bloom is the character in James Joyce's novel Ulysses who gives its closing soliloquy.

clue.text: Material under a pound's excellent

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the excellent word below the pound letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A fabric costing under a pound is excellent value.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate open fabric.

clue.text: Experienced, but left out?

annotationWithheld.why: Experienced, but left out? for PELT: experienced suggests FELT, and no parse found for P or for 'left out'; the first letter is unchecked, so the answer itself may be FELT

clue.text: Cow tucked into grain as main source of food?

indicators.note: tucked into says the first piece goes inside the grain word

parts.note: a seed is a grain
to cow is to intimidate, to awe

explanation.surface: A cow tucks into grain, its chief source of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is an old poetic word for the sea, so the definition is food from the sea; 'tucked into' puts the cow word inside the grain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is a food plant gathered from the sea, the main.

clue.text: Risk the introduction of laywomen in part of the church

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: It is risky to bring laywomen into a part of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: A fresh flower opening

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky, impudent, means pert
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A newly opened bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (it flows): the Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, an opening.

clue.text: Remarkable occurrence seen 1995 but not 1996

parts.note: 1995 is an odd-numbered year and 1996 an even one, so the quality in question belongs to the first year only

explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a strange or peculiar occurrence or thing.
